title: Best practices
intro: Everyday mistakes that make workloads fragile or wasteful, checked on the pod templates of workloads and on what surrounds them: autoscalers, disruption budgets, LimitRanges and where the replicas run. A check that needs something Sextant cannot read is skipped. Nothing is changed in the cluster: a suggested fix is copied as YAML.

settings.title: Best-practice checks
settings.excludedHint: One name per line, or separated by spaces or commas. Excluded namespaces are left out of the page, the details and the problems.

readinessProbe.title: No readiness probe
readinessProbe.why: Without a readiness probe a pod gets traffic as soon as its containers start, before the application is ready, and a rollout goes on even when the new pods cannot serve. The container declares port {{port}}, so it serves something.

livenessProbe.title: No liveness probe
livenessProbe.why: Without a liveness probe a container that hangs without exiting is never restarted. Let the probe check only the process itself, not its dependencies: otherwise a slow database restarts healthy pods.

mutableImage.title: Image without a pinned version
mutableImage.why: An image tagged latest, or without a tag, can change under the same name: new pods may run code nobody deployed, and a rollback brings back the newest image instead of the old one.

pullAlwaysDigest.title: Image pinned by digest is pulled on every start
pullAlwaysDigest.why: An image pinned by digest never changes, so imagePullPolicy Always only adds a request to the registry on every start, and pods cannot start while the registry is unreachable.

singleReplica.title: Single replica
singleReplica.why: With one replica every restart, eviction, node drain and rollout is downtime.
singleReplica.whyHpa: HorizontalPodAutoscaler {{hpa}} may scale it down to one replica: then every restart, eviction, node drain and rollout is downtime.

noPdb.title: No PodDisruptionBudget
noPdb.why: Without a PodDisruptionBudget a node drain or a cluster upgrade may evict every replica at once. A budget makes evictions wait until enough replicas are ready.

pdbBlocksDisruption.title: PodDisruptionBudget allows no disruption
pdbBlocksDisruption.why: PodDisruptionBudget {{pdb}} lets no pod be evicted (expected pods: {{pods}}): node drains and cluster upgrades stop until the budget is changed or deleted.

sameNode.title: All replicas on one node
sameNode.why: The running replicas ({{count}}) are all on node {{node}}: when that node fails or is drained, the workload is down. Topology spread constraints or pod anti-affinity make the scheduler place replicas on different nodes.

noRequests.title: No resource requests
noRequests.why: Without requests the scheduler places the pod as if it needed nothing: nodes get overcommitted, and the pod is among the first to be evicted when a node runs short of memory.

noMemoryLimit.title: No memory limit
noMemoryLimit.why: Without a memory limit a leaking container can take all the memory of its node and get other pods evicted or killed. A CPU limit is not asked for: it throttles the container even when the node has CPU to spare.

limitsAboveRecommendation.title: Limit far above the right-sizing recommendation
limitsAboveRecommendation.why: The limit is more than twice the recommendation from the usage history ({{recommended}}): the node must keep room for usage that never comes, and a runaway container can grow far before it is stopped.

hpaMinEqualsMax.title: HorizontalPodAutoscaler cannot scale
hpaMinEqualsMax.why: HorizontalPodAutoscaler {{hpa}} has the same minimum and maximum ({{min}}), so it never scales: raise the maximum, or remove the autoscaler and set the replicas.
